subject: Postcall: clarifying capacity profile & fastest-fallback plan for ShopSwift
body:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Hughes <elliot.hughes@shopswift.com>; Priya Menon <priya.menon@shopswift.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0400
Subject: Postcall: clarifying capacity profile & fastest-fallback plan for ShopSwift

Hi Elliot / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and the questions we promised to follow up on so we can recommend the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private VPC).

Call recap (short):
- Primary feature: real-time product search completions + reranking that power autocompletion and personalized suggestions.
- Current traffic profile: baseline traffic from search endpoints with spiky peaks around promotions.
- Key constraint: tail latency for interactive flows — product detail/autocomplete must feel instant.

Questions we need to finalize recommendation:
1) Typical request shape (avg tokens in / out): ~? average input ~45 tokens, avg generated ~25 tokens?
2) Baseline and peak QPS / concurrency: average QPS now and 95th/99th peak QPS during promotions.
3) SLO targets (p95, p99) — what are acceptable thresholds for product UX?
4) Acceptable maintenance windows / data residency must-haves for Private VPC?

Preliminary guidance from our side: if you need consistent p99 < 300ms at peak and predictable throughput during promos, Dedicated is the safer choice (reserved GPU pool + autoscaling). Hosted can often hit low median latency with caching and short prefixes but has more variation under noisy multi-tenant peaks unless we design a fallback.

Suggested next steps:
- Elliot: send the numbers for QPS (baseline / peak), average tokens, and one example of a heavy day (CSV or brief notes).
- We’ll thread in Ben (SE) for an initial Dedicated sizing estimate and a Hosted-fallback design that keeps the app responsive if Dedicated saturates.
- We can run a 2-week pilot on a small Dedicated pool (non-prod traffic) and capture p50/p95/p99 across your real queries.

Attachments: scope doc and draft Dedicated config attached.

Thanks — I’ll put a calendar invite for a 30-minute sizing sync once we have the QPS numbers.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: shop-swift-ma-scope.pdf (PDF, 127KB)]

From: Elliot Hughes <elliot.hughes@shopswift.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@shopswift.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 16:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Postcall: clarifying capacity profile & fastest-fallback plan for ShopSwift

Lauren —

Appreciate the summary. Answers inline below.

1) Tokens: average user query ~35 tokens, response ~18 tokens. Heavier flows (product description expansion) up to 120 tokens output.
2) QPS: baseline 18 QPS across two regions; during campaigns we spike to ~240 QPS sustained for 10-20 minute windows, with brief microbursts hitting ~430 QPS for ~30–60s.
3) SLOs: target p95 < 200ms for autocomplete; p99 ideally < 450ms but we can accept up to 600ms for more complex outputs.
4) Data residency: must remain in us-east region; no on-prem requirement today.

Priority: minimize customer-visible latency for autocomplete. We want predictable behavior during campaign peaks even if it costs a bit more.

Attaching a short CSV with a sample 24h QPS distribution.

Thanks,
Elliot
Senior Engineering Manager, ShopSwift
[Attachment: shopswift_qps_sample.csv (CSV, 64KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elliot Hughes <elliot.hughes@shopswift.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@shopswift.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 17:00:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Postcall: clarifying capacity profile & fastest-fallback plan for ShopSwift

Thanks for the data, Elliot — very helpful. High-level technical read:

- Traffic profile indicates medium baseline with short intense bursts (sub-minute) up to ~430 QPS. Those microbursts will be the deciding factor.
- Recommendation: Dedicated reserved capacity sized for sustained promo spikes (target headroom ~20–30% above sustained peak 240 QPS). For the very short microbursts, add a Hosted fallback route configured to accept overflow with degraded routing rules (e.g., reduced max output tokens, lower top_p/temperature for cost/throughput benefits).

Sizing note (ballpark):
- If we assume 35 input + 18 output tokens average, with our optimized kernels and batching, a 4-GPU Dedicated pool with burst autoscaling to 6 GPUs should provide stable p99 headroom for the sustained 240 QPS and keep p95 under 200ms. Exact sizing depends on model choice and quantization.

Operational plan:
1) Pilot: 2-week Dedicated pilot provisioned in us-east with canary traffic (10–20% of production) + synthetic loads to exercise promo spikes.
2) Fallback: configure Hosted overflow with throttling policies and a fast-path prefix cache to keep autocomplete tolerable when Dedicated is saturated.
3) Eval: collect p50/p95/p99 and token cost per 1M tokens; review after pilot and finalize contract.

I’ve attached a quick config workbook with example GPU counts and expected latency curves. Happy to run through in the sizing sync.

- Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-dedicated-config.xlsx (XLSX, 86KB)]
